我去！华尔街量化基金花几百万年薪养的那帮研究员，手里最核心的武器——强化学习交易框架，被哥伦比亚大学团队直接开源了！

FinRL，16.4K stars，全球首个金融强化学习开源框架。

以前想用强化学习做量化交易，要么从零搭 Gym 环境，要么照着论文自己造轮子。

FinRL 不一样，2020 年哥大团队开源，把「数据 → 训练 → 测试 → 交易」做成标准流水线，还带 15 个现成数据源。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 完整训练链路：数据处理、特征工程、训练、测试、回测，一套流程直接串起来

2️⃣ 内置 A2C、DDPG、PPO、TD3、SAC 等主流 DRL 算法，可以在同一市场环境里直接比较

3️⃣ 支持单股交易、多股票组合、资产配置、Crypto、A 股等不同金融任务

4️⃣ 市场环境会考虑交易成本、风险指标和仓位变化，不只是简单预测下一根 K 线

5️⃣ 自带 Benchmark，可以把强化学习策略和 DJIA、均值方差优化等传统方法放在一起比较

6️⃣ Jupyter 教程很多，从数据下载、训练 Agent 到回测结果，适合直接拆代码学整套流程

我觉得 FinRL 最有意思的地方，是它换了一个问题。

传统模型问：“明天涨还是跌？”

FinRL 问：“在不断变化的市场里，现在到底该买多少、卖多少、还是继续持有？”

这才是强化学习真正适合交易的地方。

做强化学习量化、AI Trading Agent，或者想系统研究 DRL 怎么真正接进交易的，这个值得收藏。

https://t.co/FwFYHeeAae

卧槽！量化圈最烧钱的 KDB+，被这个开源时序数据库平替了

QuestDB，17.4K stars，Apache-2.0 开源。tick 数据 / 行情 / 回测存储一把梭。

金融 tick 数据又大又密，传统数据库存不动，机构清一色上 KDB+，授权贵得离谱。

QuestDB 不一样，2014 年做到现在的开源老牌，零 GC Java + C++/Rust 热路径，专为低延迟时序设计。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 专门为 Tick、Order Book、Trades 这种高频时间序列设计，乱序写入、去重、WAL 都直接处理

2️⃣ 新增 QWP 二进制协议，一条连接同时负责写入和查询，官方峰值达到 1900 万行/秒

3️⃣ SQL 直接为量化准备了 SAMPLE BY、ASOF JOIN、LATEST ON、WINDOW JOIN，算 OHLCV、盘口匹配很顺手

4️⃣ Live Views + Materialized Views 可以边接实时行情边计算指标，不用每次重新扫完整历史数据

5️⃣ 原生支持 Parquet、Arrow、PostgreSQL 协议，Python、Pandas、Polars、Grafana 这些都能直接接

6️⃣ 新版加入 QuestDB Skill + MCP，Claude、Codex、Cursor 可以自己查 Schema、写 SQL、分析行情，甚至搭实时 Dashboard

每秒摄入百万级事件、毫秒查实时数据，而且现在连 Claude、Codex、Cursor 都能直接接。

我觉得它现在最有意思的地方，是已经不只是“一个很快的时序数据库”。

它开始往 AI Agent 的实时金融数据底座走了。

上面 Agent 做研究、策略和分析，下面 QuestDB 负责把几亿条 Tick、订单簿和历史行情稳稳托住。

做量化交易、Crypto 行情、订单簿研究、高频数据，或者想给自己的 AI Trading Agent 搭数据底座，这个值得留着。

https://t.co/pdKqgTLo3a

text:
A flight attendant who's worked 11,000+ flights over 14 years told me:

"Every passenger on this plane paid a different price for the same seat. The person in 14A paid $189. The person in 14B paid $412. Same flight. Same legroom. Same peanuts."

"Airlines don't have one price. They have 15–20 fare classes per flight each with a different price for the same seat. The price you see depends on when you search, what day you fly, how far out you book, what device you search on, and how much demand the algorithm predicts for that flight."

"The person who paid $189 didn't find a coupon. Didn't use a hack. Didn't have a connection at the airline. They understood 10 things about how airlines price, sell, and fill seats and searched accordingly."

"The person who paid $412 googled 'flights to Chicago,' clicked the first result, booked on a Friday, for a Sunday departure, 5 days out, and accepted whatever price appeared."

"Same flight. Same seat. $223 difference. And that difference happens on every flight, every day, across every airline in the world."

Bayern officials met with Michael Olise’s agent, Glen Tweneboah, in Munich to discuss how to better project his client’s image publicly, in a way that would also benefit the club. The aim was for the Frenchman to present himself more openly at marketing and sponsorship events, for example. The club wanted to understand why Olise keeps such a low profile in public and sometimes makes rather bizarre appearances. Since that meeting, there has been even bigger satisfaction with Olise internally, as he has made a stronger effort to represent Bayern positively 

Teammates and club employees report that Olise presents himself completely differently within the club. There, he's funny and well-liked, particularly in the dressing room. His teammates have noticed that Olise has a major problem letting unfamiliar people get close to him. He needs a long time to build trust with people, even within the club. Only once he manages to do that does he open up more. When it comes to people he doesn't know, such as new employees, fans or members of the media, however, he often completely shuts down 

Olise's teammates hold him in extremely high regard. The Frenchman sets an example of complete professionalism: He arrives at the training ground on Säbener Straße among the first every day, puts in extra work on the pitch and in the gym, and is regarded as an extremely ambitious player and person.

I saw Tibo at a grocery store in San Francisco yesterday. I told him how cool it was to meet him in person, but I didn’t want to be a douche and bother him and ask him for resets or anything.

He said, “Oh, like you’re doing now?”

I was taken aback, and all I could say was “Huh?” but he kept cutting me off and going “huh? huh? huh?” and closing his hand shut in front of my face. I walked away and continued with my shopping, and I heard him chuckle as I walked off. When I came to pay for my stuff up front I saw him trying to walk out the doors with like fifteen Milky Ways in his hands without paying.

The girl at the counter was very nice about it and professional, and was like “Sir, you need to pay for those first.” At first he kept pretending to be tired and not hear her, but eventually turned back around and brought them to the counter.

When she took one of the bars and started scanning it multiple times, he stopped her and told her to scan them each individually “to prevent any cache infetterence,” and then turned around and winked at me. I don’t even think that’s a word. After she scanned each bar and put them in a bag and started to say the price, he kept interrupting her by yawning really loudly.

如果手里有 2 万 U，靠 LP 一个月赚 1 万人民币，你还会上班吗？

最近美股 LP 特别火。
有人 2 万 U 做 LP，每天躺赚50U。
有人半个月赚了 4 万 U，不到三个月做到 21 万 U。
还有人专门追着热门池子做，行情好的时候，一天光手续费就能收到上万 U。

我把最近看到的 LP 内容整理了一遍，直接把有用的放这里。

1、LP 到底赚什么钱？

其实很好理解，你往池子里放两种资产，给别人提供交易需要的流动性，别人来买卖，每发生一笔交易都会产生手续费，其中一部分就会分给提供流动性的人。

比如一个池子今天成交了 1000 万 U，手续费率 0.3%，那一天就会产生 3 万 U 手续费，再按照协议规则分给池子里的 LP。

所以 LP 赚的就是交易产生的手续费，交易越活跃，产生的手续费越多，LP 能分到的钱自然也越多。

2、为什么最近美股 LP 这么火？

因为美股开始往链上搬了。以前做 LP主要围着 ETH、SOL、Meme 和各种新币，现在 Google、Amazon、NVDA 这些美股资产也开始进入链上市场。

只要有人买、有人卖，中间就有手续费，交易量起来了，手续费自然也跟着起来。

3、新手想系统学习LP，一定不能错过的几位博主

1、@ZhanweiC  ZC 老师
不到 3000 U 做到 5480 U。

只挑自己长期看好的美股，价格跌下来的时候用 LP 接盘，一边接货，一边赚 fee。
现在低位接 Google，每天躺着赚钱
https://t.co/aEBcI3jSZ0

2、 @BlockBloomer  青蛙老师
LP 基础知识 + 实战问题整理。

最通俗的把 LP 比成摆摊：有人交易就收手续费，但手里的货也会跌，换区间也有成本。
https://t.co/Fnny0u1yk2

3、@SUOHA_AI 梭哈老师
超详细的LP / 套利实战资料库。

把 @gch_enbsbxbs CJ 老师过去所有公开的 LP、套利内容分类整理到了一起，直接拿来当资料库翻。

1 万 USDG 做 Robinhood Chain LP，一个月赚 2 万美元的男人。

作为全网最早一批使用上 UltraFast 的Codex用户，今天我用了一天500$ plan，分享从速度、容量和智能方面的三个亲身强烈感受

我有点后怕，这种感受只有亲自使用了才懂

1/ 速度实在是太快了
GPT6 Ultra的速度和instant模式差不多了。我喜欢在等待 AI 的过程中刷刷手机。今天我手机刚一解锁，AI 就做完了，连刷手机的空档都没有

2/ 实在是太贵了
今天我大概用了 2 到 3 个小时，就把一周的额度用完了

现在大部分人面对 AI 的最大优势，就是我们比 AI 便宜，包括我在内

3/ 智能水平没得说，丝毫没有感觉到降质

text:
Two years ago, @ChengYANG_yc and I built ChartMimic (https://t.co/nEwUCQHtzy) to test whether models understand the structure behind a chart, by asking them to rebuild it in code. InfoEdit, our sequel with @lemonnoel52 , asks the harder question: can they keep that structure intact while changing it?

This matters more now. Image models draw infographics straight in pixels; slides, diagrams, even videos are increasingly written as code. Both look great on the first draft. The test is the second: in a photo, a good edit leaves the rest alone; in an infographic, the rest has to move with it.

Neither path is there yet, and they break in different places. So I don't think the answer is pixels or code. It's models that understand what they draw, however they draw it.

#EMNLP2026

quotedTweet.text:
🚀 Thrilled to introduce our work InfoEdit: Probing Global Layout Reasoning in Infographic Editing (EMNLP 2026).

AI can now help us generate posters, infographics and slides,  through image generation (Nano Banana) or code generation (Codex).

🤔But can AI faithfully edit them, whether through image editing or multimodal code editing?  When editing, one change forces the whole layout to adapt. We call this reflow, and we built InfoEdit to put it to the test.

🧩 What is reflow?
Take a simple edit: insert one new step into a cycle diagram. It sounds like adding one box. But a correct edit moves every node, reroutes every arrow, and rebalances the spacing, all while keeping existing content intact.

📊 InfoEdit at a glance
• 1,000 infographics, in HTML and PowerPoint
• 8 logical-relation families
• 4,000 editing instructions
• 4 tasks: Expand-Text  · Insert-Element  · Swap-Block  · Reshape-Canvas

😬 Image editors struggle
Across 8 frontier image editors, only GPT-Image-2 clears 60% average success; most fall below 7%. Swap-Block is the hardest: even when we mark the exact blocks to swap, no editor exceeds 35%. The bottleneck isn't finding the target. It's reflow.

🖼️ vs 💻 Pixels or code?
Editing the HTML/PPT source instead, Kimi-K3 reaches 67.9% average success, above GPT-Image-2's 62.0%, and lifts Swap-Block from 25.5% → 62.8% Yet pixel-level editing still wins on Expand-Text and Reshape-Canvas. The two paradigms are complementary.

💡 Takeaway
Editing structured visuals isn't just changing the requested edits. It takes reasoning about how the whole design should adapt.

#EMNLP #multimodal #coding #imagediting

这两天YouTube上有一个视频杀疯了，
成都女孩“墨韵”用咱们两千多年历史的古筝，
翻弹了老鹰乐队的摇滚神曲《加州旅馆》，
狂揽两千多万播放量，底下的老外在评论区直接听懵了。

《加州旅馆》最绝的就是那段吉他Solo，
而墨韵硬是用古筝清脆悠扬的拨弦声，
把这段西方摇滚的经典神仙还原了。
她用现场循环演奏的方式，
把摇滚的狂野律动和东方民乐的韵味完美融合。
很多外国网友惊呼，这绝对是他们听过最不可思议、最美妙的翻唱版本，硬生生让咱们这门历史悠久的传统乐器在全球狠狠圈了一波粉。

这段旋律对咱们在美国、尤其是德州生活的华人来说，
听着感受极其奇妙。德州本来就是一个极度热爱经典摇滚和吉他文化的地方，平时大家开着车在高速上，电台里最常放的公路神曲就是这首。但当这首刻进美国人骨子里的旋律，顺着咱们老祖宗的古筝弦流淌出来时，那种东方底蕴跟西方经典完美碰撞的感觉，
真的让人头皮发麻，又极其自豪。
我们的文化不仅能高山流水，玩起经典流行一样能惊艳世界。
https://t.co/kEMPIRe9oh

text:
Is it legal to sell product for $200/mo then decrease it's limits by 50% and act like it's fine?

Where is my refund?

quotedTweet.text:
Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

text:
为啥现在的人开始审视原生家庭？

人脑的发育状态，特别是情绪这一块。主要取决于家庭的氛围。

——爸爸妈妈天天在家里搂搂抱抱，打闹追逐。一家人吃肉跳舞看电影打游戏。

这样的家庭，由于儿童的认知系统感觉到环境的“高度协作性，高度激励性”，他的情绪状态就会异常的好。因为他吃下去的营养大脑根本不会用来发育“警觉”。心态能不好吗。我们人的压力是一个生理反应。并不是心理问题。

当一个孩子成长在一个绝对阳光且情绪高涨的环境中。他的压力器官就会非常“弱”。于是他就真的在高压环境下也会镇定自若。因为你的心态来自于你的“生理反应”。而如果你生理上压力器官就不发达。你怎样获得压力，当然就没有压力。

你去看看学校里“光芒四射”的那些孩子，基本上高中都还跟父母勾肩搭背，喊爸爸帅哥，喊妈妈美女——就是因为人的情绪系统来自于我们的生长环境。

一个人的性格，八成以上，是家庭环境的投射。

绝没有什么——我家挺好的，但孩子又冷漠又自卑又爱发脾气。没这事，你只是不愿意承认你们家的问题而已。

——传统中国家庭。命令，控制，严管，亲子关系冷漠，父母双方也冷漠，充满指责和冷暴力。

孩子在发育中，他的认知系统为了“警觉”随时可能到来的危险。就会变得异常敏感。我们的情绪系统本身就是一个“生存防御机制”，一个敏感的孩子只有两条路走，要么无限的逃避，要么暴力失控。

所以现在大家相亲的时候说，怎么排雷，怎么事先避免遇到人渣，渣男渣女。

很简单，跟对方家庭接触一下就行了。父母不对劲的，孩子绝对好不了（不是说这个人坏，父母不省事的，孩子很可能是焦虑人格。焦虑人格存在感情依恋问题——在爱情中会显得特别温柔，忠诚。但实际上长远发展会变成恶性索取和控制欲）

以上是心态。

至于特长培养。非常，非常，非常简单。

由于人脑的自然分布性，每个人擅长的事情都不一样。怎么发现这种特长。不是你看见他想画画，你就培养他画画。儿童在幼年时代为了知觉世界，形成思维基础，对任何事情都是感兴趣的，对浇水泥也有兴趣，难道你培养他做装修吗。

他想做什么，就给他机会去了解。不要管什么3分钟热度。人脑的认知系统在能够模拟一件事之后就对这件事缺乏兴趣是非常正常的——儿童买玩具就是为了模拟这件事务，一旦学会了，他就不要了。也并不是儿童对玩具缺乏责任感。

一个人的特长，会出现在———他明明了解一个事情，并且能做好。但他却“没有放弃”这才是“异常”的。放弃是正常的，不放弃才是奇怪的。他很擅长了，但没有你们的要求或者鼓励，他还是会经常做这件事。

这个，一般来说就是大脑自然分布上的优势点，就可以培养了。

比如小学一年级就学画画，你们也没有特别给他报班，要他实现什么目标，就随便玩。结果六年级了还在画画——那么就可以适当的认真培养了。

自主性不需要培养。人脑的本质就是自主性。你不“压制”就行了。 自主性不会缺乏，只会被压制。你觉得小孩子没有自主性

——那100%是你控制他过多，他变得顺从之后为了避免受到你的惩罚，自然而然地放弃了自主性。

自律性，父母以身作则就行了。儿童是环境习得性的。 环境怎样，他就怎样。你看小孩子不是经常说“凭什么隔壁的小孩儿就能玩，我就不能玩”

你看，他是从环境特点判断自己该如何约束自己的。所以如果你父母两个人只发号施令而自己缺乏相应的自我约束。

比如小孩儿不准玩手机，你俩抱着手机就不放。

那只会导致孩子认知失调，变得暴躁。对自律没什么帮助。

——那100%是你控制他过多，他变得顺从之后为了避免受到你的惩罚，自然而然地放弃了自主性。

自律性，父母以身作则就行了。儿童是环境习得性的。 环境怎样，他就怎样。你看小孩子不是经常说“凭什么隔壁的小孩儿就能玩，我就不能玩”

你看，他是从环境特点判断自己该如何约束自己的。所以如果你父母两个人只发号施令而自己缺乏相应的自我约束。

比如小孩儿不准玩手机，你俩抱着手机就不放。

那只会导致孩子认知失调，变得暴躁。对自律没什么帮助。

Emerging from my cave to share our massive DevDay today! My highlights:

# The future of work

## Dots: Remarkably capable, always on personal agents
In my product role, which is very delegatory, I pretty much only talk to dots. Use dots for delegation; Codex if you want to do something yourself. 

## Space: Collaborative workspace for humans and agents.
Dots in Space let us design each to be more opinionated like Slack vs GDocs, as opposed to ChatGPT which is somewhere between the two.

## Codex Cloud 2.0: Shut your laptop. Codex on cloud is awesome now!
Runs on the same new infra that powers dots and more. 

## Meetings Plugin
Transcribe your meetings. This is a first party example of Plugin extensions.

# Platform & infra bets

## ChatGPT [dot] com merge with desktop app
When we started building the Codex VS Code Extension, we had the ambition of a single agentic codebase across VS Code, Desktop and Web. We have it now!

## Codex Cloud Agent Runtime
This behind the scenes infra powers dots, ChatGPT Work, Agents API, and more. It lets us connect to dynamic execution environments so that dots can both think in the cloud, work in the cloud, and connect to your computer.

## Plugin extensions
Render custom UI right in the ChatGPT desktop app or web.

# Ultrafast
8x speed! (And yes 6x cost.)

text:
Netflix 用了十几年的推荐算法，被一个只会读字的 LLM 打赢了。

这玩意叫 GenRec。

以前 Netflix 的推荐是这么做的：
一大帮数据科学家，手工造几千个特征，
把你的观看行为翻译成各种数学信号。
专门的模型架构，很重的基础设施，一直有人在调。

GenRec 的做法很粗暴：
把你的观看记录和影片信息，直接写成一段自然语言。
丢给一个基础大模型去读。
一次前向计算，给整个片库打分。

没有手工特征，没有定制架构。

结果它不光追平了那套调了好多年的线上系统，还有统计显著的提升。
用的标注训练数据，大概少了 40 倍。

我觉得最狠的是这个 40 倍。
过去那几千个特征里装的“经验”，大模型读一读你的观看记录，好像自己就理解出来了。

边界也说一下：
原帖用的词是“替换”，但从描述看，是拿它和线上系统做的对比结果。
有没有全量上线、推理成本扛不扛得住，原帖没说。
Netflix 这个体量，每次推荐都让 LLM 读一遍，账单估计不会太好看。

但方向我觉得已经挺清楚了。
以前做推荐，核心手艺是把人翻译成数字。
现在变成了把人写成一段话。

感觉以后推荐算法岗面试，得加考一篇作文了。

https://t.co/Td44iNE24X

quotedTweet.text:
Netflix replaced their 15 years old recommendation algorithm with an LLM.

It’s called "GenRec" and it completely changes how recommendation algorithms are built.

For over a decade, the Netflix recommendation engine was a masterclass in feature engineering. Data scientists built thousands of complex, handcrafted features to figure out what you wanted to watch next.

It required bespoke architectures. Massive infrastructure. Constant manual tuning.

Netflix threw all of it away.

They built GenRec, an LLM-backed ranker.

Instead of translating your behavior into complex math, they just turn your watch history and metadata into a natural language sentence.

They feed that raw text into a foundation LLM.

The AI simply reads your behavior like a story, understands your evolving tastes, and scores the entire catalog in a single forward pass.

No manual feature engineering. No complex bespoke architectures.

Here is the part that should terrify traditional data scientists.

This text-based LLM didn't just match the highly tuned production system Netflix spent years perfecting.

It beat it.

And it achieved those statistically significant gains using roughly 40x fewer labeled training examples.

We are watching a massive paradigm shift in real time.

The most complex predictive algorithms in the world are being replaced by models that just know how to read.

If Netflix can replace their core product engine with an LLM, what complex system in your business is about to become obsolete?

text:
今天晚上 10 点，我的 Claude 老号毫无征兆被封了。

用了大半年，一直为了这个账号小心翼翼供着原生家宽 IP。
并且这个账号过kyc后买来一路从免费版升级：

$20 尝鲜
$100 重度主力使用了好几个月
最后开到顶配 $200

结果 $200 还没 $100 用得久，用了不满两个月直接阵亡。

我第一反应先是骂A ÷玄学风控、同时怀疑自己节点是否被标记不干净。
但静下心拉了 Clash 的连接日志，把 Mac 上的路由表、DNS 和后台进程彻底摸了一遍，我服了。

面对AI风控,现在大部分教程都在疯狂教你折腾“纯净住宅 IP”。
其实真正害死账号的，往往是本地网络环境的“精神分裂”。

这里我实践排查出来的 3 个致命硬伤：

1.Claude Code 压根不支持 SOCKS很多人随手配个 socks5 变量，但官方文档写得清清楚楚：只认 HTTP_PROXY 和 HTTPS_PROXY，不支持 SOCKS。配错了对应出口后它根本不认，流量直接裸奔或异常打架。

2.IPv4 和 IPv6 严重割裂IPv4 规规矩矩走了家宽节点，IPv6 却在本地直连或者经由不同的虚拟网卡分流。在服务端眼里，你相当于上一秒在美国，下一秒直接瞬移。

3.终端、桌面端、浏览器出口完全不一致CLI 终端走一套环境变量，桌面端走 TUN，浏览器还带着残留的动态端口后台重启。同一个账号，几个客户端同时挂着完全不同的出口在调用。

所以说原生家宽固然重要。
但本地网络没有对齐，IP 买再贵也是白送。

所以如果你也是AI重度用户，给几个我自己实践用过的排查建议：

明确禁用或阻断 IPv6，确保没有双栈绕过
给 Claude Code 显式配置 HTTP 代理，别依赖 SOCKS

统一所有客户端走同一条出口路径，排查并干掉后台偷跑的僵尸进程(claude codex都要监控)

---

最后祝大家的账号都安好,能够安心使用AI🫰

用了大半年，一直为了这个账号小心翼翼供着原生家宽 IP。
并且这个账号过kyc后买来一路从免费版升级：

$20 尝鲜
$100 重度主力使用了好几个月
最后开到顶配 $200

结果 $200 还没 $100 用得久，用了不满两个月直接阵亡。

我第一反应先是骂A ÷玄学风控、同时怀疑自己节点是否被标记不干净。
但静下心拉了 Clash 的连接日志，把 Mac 上的路由表、DNS 和后台进程彻底摸了一遍，我服了。

面对AI风控,现在大部分教程都在疯狂教你折腾“纯净住宅 IP”。
其实真正害死账号的，往往是本地网络环境的“精神分裂”。

这里我实践排查出来的 3 个致命硬伤：

1.Claude Code 压根不支持 SOCKS很多人随手配个 socks5 变量，但官方文档写得清清楚楚：只认 HTTP_PROXY 和 HTTPS_PROXY，不支持 SOCKS。配错了对应出口后它根本不认，流量直接裸奔或异常打架。

2.IPv4 和 IPv6 严重割裂IPv4 规规矩矩走了家宽节点，IPv6 却在本地直连或者经由不同的虚拟网卡分流。在服务端眼里，你相当于上一秒在美国，下一秒直接瞬移。

3.终端、桌面端、浏览器出口完全不一致CLI 终端走一套环境变量，桌面端走 TUN，浏览器还带着残留的动态端口后台重启。同一个账号，几个客户端同时挂着完全不同的出口在调用。

所以说原生家宽固然重要。
但本地网络没有对齐，IP 买再贵也是白送。

所以如果你也是AI重度用户，给几个我自己实践用过的排查建议：

明确禁用或阻断 IPv6，确保没有双栈绕过
给 Claude Code 显式配置 HTTP 代理，别依赖 SOCKS

统一所有客户端走同一条出口路径，排查并干掉后台偷跑的僵尸进程(claude codex都要监控)

---

最后祝大家的账号都安好,能够安心使用AI🫰

i still don't understand why everyone is NOT using this 100% free alternative to TradingView

it does everything TradingView charges $2,399/year for FREE

i plugged openmarket into my Opus 5.5 + Jev stack and built an ORDER FLOW trading desk that is running autonomously 24/7

here is the EXACT system you can build today:

1. openmarket streams three things live for free, the liquidation heatmap, the order book depth, and CVD, the exact order flow a fund pays thousands for

2. the liquidation map shows where the stops are stacked, price hunts those clusters, so it tells you where the market wants to go next

3. the order book shows if there is more size on the buy or the sell side, that is who is actually in control right now

4. CVD shows if the buying is real, price up but CVD down means the move is fake and about to fail, the read most people never see

5. i pull all three through the OpenMarket API and pack them into one clean snapshot on every candle

6. Jev scores that snapshot in < 100 ms, is a cluster about to get hunted, is the flow real or fading, buy sell or hold

7. Opus 5.5 sits on top, after fixed time it reads which order flow reads actually worked and rewrites the questions Jev asks, so it gets sharper and becomes powerful itself

8. a hard risk layer holds every limit and now the desk trades institutional order flow on its own, for ZERO dollars a month in data

the full build is in my article below:

1）一张 Bank Reset，额度重置卡。

失望，以及今天的Codex，速度更慢了，消耗更快了，我只是修一个小地方+鹈鹕测试，就消耗了4%！

text:
jev + sonnet 5.5 is f**king insane.

my entire workflow got 4x faster after adding these 6 lines to CLAUDE.md.

[with jev connected, paste this👇]

1. Before you start a Claude worker, ask Jev once to select a host-approved profile with one or two sessions. The profile must specify each session’s model and effort level. If Jev makes no selection, use the host default.

2. The host must check Jev’s selection. The host must set the model and effort before each session starts. Keep these settings fixed during the session. The host controls permissions and approvals.

3. Use Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort for clear coding tasks. Use higher effort for complex reasoning or JSON tasks. Use a second Claude only for independent research or a review that the user requested.

4. Give the second Claude the task, applicable files, limits, and completion requirements. Return its findings and evidence to the lead.

5. Complete the requested work. Ask the user only when you cannot continue without input or before an action that needs approval. Do not add features, tests, files, documentation, refactors, or review rounds that the user did not request. When the work is complete and checked, stop. Report the result.

6. Before you report completion, run a test, build, type check, or command that checks the code change. If no check can run, identify the missing check. Explain why it cannot run.

same task. two timers. watch the difference.

quotedTweet.text:
Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

company OS (org harness) vs personal agent, similarities and differences:

differences:
- Many principals (users), one actor (agent): will need to be multiplayer, handle multiple users (sometimes even in same thread), and as a result handle auth/memory correctly
- governance: observability, auditability, admin control plane matter way more
- interaction pattern: more event driven and async

similarities:
- should be able to write/execute code
- browser use likely very important! (key difference from a coding harness)
- skills/MCP as standards
- core agent loop/logic

what am i missing?

text:
我其实情商一直挺低的，不太会说话。

当年在上海做项目，甲方有位女负责人，穿搭新潮，每天打扮都不一样。

我们在工作上经常意见不合，没少吵架。

一次饭局喝了点酒，我随口吐槽她：看她那样都三十多了，还总把自己当成刚毕业的小姑娘，太能装了！

饭桌上甲方的人只是笑笑，没接话。后来再有分歧，她不再和我争执，只是冷静讲道理。

快到项目验收的时候，她单独叫我过去。我还以为是要怎么为难我，没想到她拿出一套衣服送给我，说我平常穿的太差了，别影响明天项目验收。

结果第二天项目顺利验收，公司领导也夸我，说甲方对我评价很好。

过了很久我才知道，这位女士已经48岁，孩子都大学毕业了。

Each agent is a slash command in plain Markdown with its own role and rules. 134k stars, MIT.

> 6 for product planning
> 6 for design
> 6 for memory and retros
> 5 for code review and debugging
> 5 for security and guardrails
> 5 for QA and performance
> 5 for shipping and deploy

They hand work to each other. /office-hours writes a design doc, the plan reviewers read it, /qa and /ship check against it.

text:
数学描述世界，计算描述过程，信息描述不确定性，动力系统描述变化，统计物理描述涌现，神经科学描述智能，科学哲学约束我们如何知道自己是对的。

如果研究者是我们必然选择的路，那不要一上来读很多思想类畅销书。冯·诺依曼与图灵共同的底层语言首先是数学。
数学读到最后，我们应该逐渐产生一种习惯。看到一个神经科学问题，第一反应是找到变量，状态空间，动力学，目标函数。
这一步会极大改变科研思维。

只学 Python、C++是不够的，那只是工具。
Alan Turing的《On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem》是必须要读的。
我们逐渐发现，图灵的问题和现代神经科学的问题其实会相遇：大脑，究竟在计算什么？

信息论是本科必须打通的副本之一。
从 Claude Shannon 的 《A Mathematical Theory of Communication》开始，然后系统读《Cover & Thomas：Elements of Information Theory》，至少我们要理解entropy，cross-entropy，KL divergence，mutual information、channel capacity，rate-distortion，把问题一路迁移到神经编码、representation learning、BCI、predictive coding、金融市场、复杂系统、AI。

这是将数学、计算、信息论、动力系统、统计物理和神经科学互相翻译的过程。
但请不要变成知识收藏家，有价值的永远是T-shaped structure。

• 新版美国护照 “Flight of the Eagle”：2028 年开始启用的新设计

整个发布方式不像政府发布政策，更像 Apple 在发布一个新产品。

text:
最近 $QQQI 非常火，它的派息率可達到 14%！
甚至有人說，買一萬股 QQQI 就可以退休了。

我想說的是，所有 Covered Cal l策略的 ETF，它們本質上是把未來的漲幅，折算成現金給你。準確地說，是把未來上漲的權利賣給了買方，收取權利金分配給你。

你獲得了它 14% 的派息，作為代價，實際上你是讓渡了未來的漲幅。然而，你拿到的這筆現金，卻不足以對沖它全部的下跌。如果市場持續下跌、走入熊市，QQQI 也會持續下跌。

金融市場任何策略都有代價。

如果你看中了QQQI 14%的派息率，代價就是，它在牛市中會大幅落後 QQQ，在熊市中跌幅卻沒有比 QQQ 少太多，搞清楚這一點就夠了。

如果你想獲得未來增值的潛力，就應該投資 $QQQ ，除非你有辦法把 QQQI 的派息做出高於 QQQ 未來漲幅的收益，否則我認為簡單持有 QQQI 的意義不大。

總之，想清楚你要什麼，漲幅和派息不可兼得。

我的兩個公開組合中都配置有 Covered call 策略ETF：
1. Hi5組合中我使用 $QQQI ，每月的派息有一部分拿去買入 $SPMO 這個進攻型極強的標的；
2. TQQQ組合中，我配置了 $JEPQ ，它的派息是用來買入進攻型更強的 $TQQQ 。

這兩個組合的連結在評論區中👇

text:
华尔街不会主动告诉你的10个免费美股网站

别再只会刷财经新闻了。

很多时候，当你看到一条新闻冲进去的时候，真正影响股价的数据，专业投资者可能早就在跟踪。

分享10个值得收藏的网站👇

1、MacroMicro：把宏观数据直接变成图

如果你看FRED觉得太硬核，可以试试MacroMicro。

通胀、利率、美债、美元、就业、制造业、流动性等大量宏观指标都做成了可视化图表。

研究“为什么美股最近涨/跌”，经常能在这里找到宏观线索。

https://t.co/lIox5txzq0

2、New York Fed：盯美元流动性

纽约联储官网是很多人容易忽略的宝藏。

SOFR、回购市场、纽约联储公开市场操作等数据，都可以直接查。

尤其当市场开始讨论“流动性”“降息”“资金面”的时候，别只看别人解读，可以回来找原始数据。

https://t.co/C0PyZ4iBzl

3、Federal Reserve：直接看美联储

研究美股，美联储官网其实应该放进收藏夹。

FOMC声明、会议纪要、经济预测、利率决议以及美联储官员相关信息，都可以找到。

不要只看新闻标题里的“鹰派”“鸽派”，原文往往比二手解读更重要。

https://t.co/vi3zz8xl2F

4、FINRA：查市场监管和交易数据

FINRA是美国金融业监管局。

除了监管信息之外，还能查询部分市场统计、OTC和交易相关数据。

当你研究一些成交异常、做空或者市场结构问题时，它比普通财经网站更接近数据源头。

https://t.co/1UTUXi4COS

5、ChartExchange：研究做空和市场数据

这个网站很多普通投资者没用过。

可以辅助查看Short Volume、Fails-to-Deliver等市场数据，一些股票还能进一步观察借券相关信息。

研究热门股、逼空概念股时，比只看社交媒体喊“Short Squeeze”靠谱得多。

https://t.co/BMfTF60ata

6、AlphaQuery：查波动率和期权数据

如果你开始研究期权，这个网站值得收藏。

可以辅助查看股票的历史波动率、隐含波动率以及部分期权统计数据。

有时候股价没怎么动，但期权市场已经开始给未来波动重新定价了。

https://t.co/nLESJsVhY5

7、StockCharts：老牌技术分析网站

界面看起来可能没有那么“新”，但工具很成熟。

趋势、均线、RSI、MACD、相对强弱等技术分析都能做。

特别适合同时观察指数、行业ETF和个股之间的强弱关系。

https://t.co/yAojQD7ZQs

8、HedgeFollow：看机构13F持仓

想知道大型基金公开披露了哪些股票，可以看看HedgeFollow。

可以追踪部分机构投资者的13F持仓以及持仓变化，用来寻找研究线索很方便。

但一定记住：

13F不是实时交易记录。

你今天看到的持仓，不代表机构今天还在同样的位置。

https://t.co/dsF52IBpjX

9、Quiver Quantitative：看另类数据

这个网站比较有意思。

除了传统股票数据之外，还整理了美国国会议员交易、企业游说、政府合同等另类数据。

这些数据不能直接告诉你股票会不会涨，但可以提供传统财报之外的研究视角。

https://t.co/AEmNi4CIj0

10、EIA：研究能源股必备

做石油、天然气、能源股，却不知道EIA，很多研究其实只做了一半。

美国原油库存、汽油库存、天然气库存、产量、进出口等能源数据，都可以直接查。

研究XOM、CVX以及油服、天然气相关公司时非常实用。

https://t.co/cKUpZiUhz6

最后提醒一句：

工具的价值，不是替你做决定，而是帮助你获得更完整的信息。

别人看新闻，你可以回到原始数据；

别人听市场传闻，你可以自己验证；

别人只看股价，你可以同时研究基本面、宏观、资金和市场预期。

真正拉开差距的，往往不是知道多少个网站，而是能不能建立自己的研究框架和判断体系。

本文仅用于信息分享与学习交流，不构成任何投资建议。

quotedTweet.text:
做美股连这10个网站都不知道，先别急着拿真金白银进场交学费！

1、TradingView：看K线和技术面非常顺手，支持多周期图表、技术指标、选股器、热力图以及价格提醒，做趋势跟踪和关键价位监控效率很高。
https://t.co/0J0oBWPS4H

2、SEC EDGAR：美国证监会官方披露系统，10-K、10-Q、8-K、Form 4等公司文件都能直接查。研究一家公司，与其只看别人总结，不如学会回到原始公告。
https://t.co/kWKQeyOJFX

3、TIKR：偏基本面深度研究，财务三表、估值倍数、分析师一致预期、电话会记录、机构持仓和全球选股器都能查，特别适合做公司和同行横向对比。
https://t.co/VXv8sjZXST

4、Quartr：财报季非常好用，可以集中查看公司电话会、历史文字稿、投资者演示材料和公告，还能搜索管理层过去说过什么，研究公司预期变化很方便。
https://t.co/tukC6ky2kH

5、CME FedWatch：专门观察市场对美联储加息、降息以及维持利率不变的预期。做美股一定要知道市场当前到底在交易怎样的利率路径。
https://t.co/hjdBcXuL1k

6、Cboe：想研究VIX和美股期权，这个网站值得常看。VIX、期权成交量、Put/Call Ratio以及波动率相关数据都能找到，适合辅助观察市场风险偏好。
https://t.co/QkUl1VizGq

7、WhaleWisdom：专门追踪机构13F持仓，可以查看基金历史持仓、增减仓以及多家机构的共同持仓，研究“聪明钱”在配置什么很方便，不过13F存在披露时滞。
https://t.co/CjXXARvbJP

8、OpenInsider：专门整理SEC Form 4内部人交易，可以筛选CEO、CFO、董事等公司内部人的买入和卖出，尤其适合寻找多人集中买入等线索。
https://t.co/XgOf6UtY0W

9、Market Chameleon：做期权和财报波动研究很好用，可以看隐含波动率、IV Rank、期权链、财报前隐含波动以及市场预期涨跌幅。
https://t.co/66XJlnQd3w

10、Portfolio Visualizer：用来做组合回测、资产相关性和风险分析，可以查看历史表现、最大回撤、资产配置以及蒙特卡洛模拟等数据。
https://t.co/2zrdtce5Zf

希望本次分享对你有帮助~

最后提醒一句：

工具的价值，不是替你做决定，而是帮助你获得更完整的信息。

别人看新闻，你可以回到原始数据；

别人听市场传闻，你可以自己验证；

别人只看股价，你可以同时研究基本面、宏观、资金和市场预期。

真正拉开差距的，往往不是知道多少个网站，而是能不能建立自己的研究框架和判断体系。

https://t.co/VXv8sjZXST

4、Quartr：财报季非常好用，可以集中查看公司电话会、历史文字稿、投资者演示材料和公告，还能搜索管理层过去说过什么，研究公司预期变化很方便。
https://t.co/tukC6ky2kH

5、CME FedWatch：专门观察市场对美联储加息、降息以及维持利率不变的预期。做美股一定要知道市场当前到底在交易怎样的利率路径。
https://t.co/hjdBcXuL1k

https://t.co/QkUl1VizGq

https://t.co/CjXXARvbJP

text:
整个科技圈风向都在卷大企业 AI， 结果 @Meta 的 @AIatMeta AI 掌门人 @alexandr_wang 刚刚发推说他们后台发现，把 Muse 用得最猛的， 竟然是修水管的、开农场的、开杂货店和开小餐馆的老板……
上线两周，早期用户里竟然有 1/3 直接把它绑定了商业账号。
今天 Meta 顺水推舟，直接上线了 Muse for Small Business， 一口气甩出 22 个官方连接器： Shopify、Stripe、QuickBooks、Canva、Zoom、Slack…… 把小商家的全套数字牛马直接做实了。

我把背后的逻辑和搞钱启示用大白话给大家拆一下👇
━━
1｜最反直觉的现象：用 AI 最狠的不是大厂，是个体户
大厂做 AI 喜欢去找世界 500 强做大单子， 但真实世界里，最缺时间的是那些“一人身兼八职”的小老板。
官方案例里有个爱荷华州开杂货店的大叔： 每周工作 65 个小时，店里进货是他、管账是他、做促销是他、处理退款还是他。 他缺的根本不是点子，是时间。
以前大家以为 Muse 只是个帮宅男比价订外卖的玩具， 结果这些小老板早就拿它去回客户邮件、查库存、算账了。

2｜这 22 个连接器，到底解决了啥？
做过独立电商、自媒体或者小生意的朋友都懂这个痛点： 每天要在 8 个后台之间来回切—— 看销量去 Shopify，查退款去 Stripe，做海报去 Canva，记账去 QuickBooks，开会去 Zoom，内部沟通去 Slack。
现在 Muse 把它全收拢到一个对话框里： ▫️查账退款：不用登录 Stripe 后台，直接对它说“把昨天争议的那笔单子退了”，它核对完调接口执行 ▫️内容与营销：识别你的产品库存和品牌调性，直接调用 Canva 生成下周促销海报，一键推到 Instagram 商业主页 ▫️客户与日程：给它配个专属邮箱，客户发来的询价、改期邮件，它在后台看懂日历直接起草回复
一句话：它不是让你去学一个新软件，而是把你手上所有的 SaaS 变成听话的后台。

3｜Meta 这步棋最狠的地方在哪？
Facebook 和 Instagram 上有整整 2 亿小微商家。 这是全球最大的个体老板聚集地。
Meta 根本不需要跟微软、谷歌去抢那些复杂的企业级大单， 它只要让这 2 亿小老板在手机上： “少雇一个客服、少花 2 小时对账、少切 5 个软件”。
而且最聪明的是它的安全机制： 所有涉及扣费、退款、对外公开发布的操作，AI 负责跑腿起草，最后一步依然要人点确认。 这就是我们常说的“人管方向和钱包，AI 管繁琐和流程”。

4｜对我们普通人和超级个体意味着什么？
一人公司（One-Person Company）过去最大的瓶颈，不是你不会做核心业务，而是被杂事活活拖死。 你懂做视频，但你不想花时间回商务邮件； 你懂写代码，但你讨厌天天去处理发票和对账。
当 AI Agent 开始长出连接现实商业系统的手（Connectors）： 以前需要 3 个人支撑的微型工作室， 以后可能真的 1 个人加一个配置好的 Personal AI 就能跑起来。

5｜照例泼盆冷水
▫️这套连接器目前深度绑定的是海外生态（Shopify、Stripe、QuickBooks 等），国内主流的微店、淘宝、微信支付等生态目前还没打通； ▫️多平台授权意味着你的商业数据、客户往来都在被 AI 扫描，哪些权限给、哪些不给，依然得有边界； ▫️复杂业务逻辑的容错率低，账目核算依然需要人工定期复核，别做甩手掌柜。
━━
过去我们讨论 AI，总觉得它是高高在上的算力和算法。
 但今天 Alexandr Wang 这条推说明了一件事： AI 落地最快、最扎实的地方， 永远是帮街角那家店的老板，把今晚下班的时间提前两个小时。
开源了自定义接入平台（https://t.co/GGtFihiFNC）。 如果国内也有一个 AI 能接通你所有的工作软件，你最想让它替你干掉哪个日常琐事？ https://t.co/zrRk2zy06N

text:
the people that got https://t.co/gazdXEVMNl to #1 in chatgpt made a video explaining how to win AEO

heres everything they shared:

>AI search isnt a black box. the models rely on consensus from the open internet and u can literally view the sources chatgpt uses to form its answers

>"#1" doesnt mean winning one query. it means consistently showing up in the top 3 across dozens of different prompts

>they wrote 47+ comparison blog posts like "cal vs calendly" and "cal vs savvycal" targeting ppl who are ready to buy, not ppl who are just browsing

>they stopped writing generic informational content that AI already answers on its own. every page became product-led and problem-solving

>1 in 3 https://t.co/gazdXEVMNl sales meetings now comes from AI visibility. they track revenue changes not rankings

>youtube has a massive correlation with AI search visibility. video content is harder to fake than text and AI models trust it more. youtube is the new reddit for AEO

>they deleted thousands of thin and underperforming pages from their site. less content, better content, more traffic. sounds backwards but it works

>they use a concept called parasite SEO -> leveraging high authority platforms like youtube and linkedin to rank content faster than they could on their own domain

>mass producing thousands of AI generated articles backfires. it creates keyword cannibalization, triggers penalties, and signals low value to search engines

>AI search is winner take all. if ur not in the top 3 recommendations u basically dont exist to the user. theres no page 2

>if ur starting from zero with no budget: skip the fancy CMS. make one high quality video comparing ur product vs a competitor and make sure ur technical SEO foundation is solid. u can start with $100

this is the most transparent breakdown ive seen from a team that actually did it. not theory. results.

text:
Tony Robbins literally explained why Robin Williams achieved everything a person could want and still hung himself. It is not money. It is not fame. It is not an Oscar. It is the one skill that has no formula.

He said there are two skills in an extraordinary life. The first is the science of achievement. How to take what you envision and make it real. Most successful people master this one and stop.

The second is the art of fulfillment. Making money is a science. Feeling rich is not. Fulfillment is different for every human being alive. You cannot model it from someone else.

Williams wanted to make the whole world laugh. He did it. He wanted his own show. It was a hit. He wanted an Academy Award for drama not comedy. He won it.

He achieved everything on the list and hung himself. Robbins said he made everyone happy except himself. That is the ultimate failure.

Robbins gets calls from multi-billionaires asking for business help. Within ten minutes they admit the truth. They are miserable. They mastered the science and never started the art.

He said wealth is not a skill. It is a decision. He lives part-time in Fiji where villagers with nothing are the happiest people he knows. A wealthy American spends years planning to finally be happy. The Fijian says sit on the beach right now.

The full interview is free. It will outlast almost everything else in your feed today.

别人买的不是一张纸，而是一份能摆在家里、送给养宠朋友的体面礼物。

永远别做纯纯的 “AI 美丽废物”。找到高情绪价值的刚需场景 + 实体落地，才是普通人真正的搞钱通天路。

而且这套打法和前两天聊的「国庆儿童节日照」完全如出一辙——非常适合二三线城市和县城下沉市场，卖给宝妈和宠主，简直是轻资产降维打击！

text:
New on Noahbench ™

GPT 6.1 Sol comes in 1st on the benches. 

HOWEVER, i will not be switching to this even though its high on benches. Heres why:

Theres a concept I've been toying with behind "talent" and "smart". Its an odd one but it can be simply understood as "talent is the ability to mechanically perform", "smart is the ability to mechanically perform and understand *why* something is being done".

I think that 6.1 sol is a wonderful refinement on top of 6, however it has not increased its base smarts. 

Talented models are the absolute perfect workhorses though, these models are the ones who are cheap to run, can do something when the thinking is done for them, and accomplish the goals. 

I am pleased with the release but will not be defaulting to it. Hats off openai!

text:
GPT-6 Astra makes this AI stack look f…cking illegal

10 GitHub repos for building everything around the model

01 LangGraph
▸ https://t.co/40xDVIgL8I
→ stateful agent orchestration

02 CrewAI
▸ https://t.co/leSFAquLAW
→ multi-agent crews

BUILD THE CORE

03 AutoGen
▸ https://t.co/QmDi0xGJNz
→ event-driven agent systems

04 PydanticAI
▸ https://t.co/f27GiNAQBR
→ typed agents + structured outputs

GIVE IT MEMORY

05 Mem0
▸ https://t.co/ifCHrrB19c
→ persistent agent memory

06 Graphiti
▸ https://t.co/mNcepop8y6
→ temporal knowledge graphs

GIVE IT TOOLS

07 Composio
▸ https://t.co/2oJOJMrKYo
→ connect agents to real tools

08 E2B
▸ https://t.co/Mz2wXEtI9B
→ isolated sandboxes for agent code

MAKE IT SURVIVE

09 OpenHands
▸ https://t.co/RLP18B0zIc
→ agents that execute real software tasks

10 AgentOps
▸ https://t.co/KeBQQ77VP8
→ trace + debug agent runs

the architecture:

context → router → agent → memory → tools → execution → eval → retry

I’d split the stack like this:

brain:
LangGraph → PydanticAI → CrewAI

memory:
Mem0 → Graphiti

execution:
Composio → E2B → OpenHands

observability:
AgentOps

the f…cking interesting part isn’t adding another model

it’s everything around the model that keeps it working

the model is becoming one folder in the stack ⭣

每天定时读取新信息，自动帮我做好当天的行程规划和任务梳理，手机端准时弹出提醒。

微信群里各种通知、各种可能遗漏的客户，还有一堆邮件……

每天被这些事情浪费很多时间，还可能遗漏。

1、我用 Skills 解密本地微信数据，让它读取到微信最新信息，同时将工作邮箱和日历授权给它，它在后台跑定时任务，每天定时抓取最新上下文，自动做好统筹和规划，手机端直接推送执行建议。
2、并且设置了定时任务，每天早晨 8 点，Today 自动结合昨天的微信沟通、新邮件和今日日程，生成报告，以及待办的任务，并在手机上提醒我。
3、定期扫描邮箱账单，定期自动检查收据，帮我翻出了在吃灰的会员，并且差旅发票和报销凭证随手发过去，自动按项目归类核对金额，省下大把时间。
4、而且，健康饮食和健身规划也都可以交给它，做好定时任务和长期规划，接着就可以开始健康生活了～
5、除此之外，这是国内第一个真正意义上的 Personal AI，电脑端在后台跑任务，手机端实时收提醒，非常方便。

国内版基础版免费用，新用户注册送 1 亿 Token 和 1 个月 Pro。

text:
卧槽！量化圈最烧钱的 KDB+，被这个开源时序数据库平替了

QuestDB，17.4K stars，Apache-2.0 开源。tick 数据 / 行情 / 回测存储一把梭。

金融 tick 数据又大又密，传统数据库存不动，机构清一色上 KDB+，授权贵得离谱。

QuestDB 不一样，2014 年做到现在的开源老牌，零 GC Java + C++/Rust 热路径，专为低延迟时序设计。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 专门为 Tick、Order Book、Trades 这种高频时间序列设计，乱序写入、去重、WAL 都直接处理

2️⃣ 新增 QWP 二进制协议，一条连接同时负责写入和查询，官方峰值达到 1900 万行/秒

3️⃣ SQL 直接为量化准备了 SAMPLE BY、ASOF JOIN、LATEST ON、WINDOW JOIN，算 OHLCV、盘口匹配很顺手

4️⃣ Live Views + Materialized Views 可以边接实时行情边计算指标，不用每次重新扫完整历史数据

5️⃣ 原生支持 Parquet、Arrow、PostgreSQL 协议，Python、Pandas、Polars、Grafana 这些都能直接接

6️⃣ 新版加入 QuestDB Skill + MCP，Claude、Codex、Cursor 可以自己查 Schema、写 SQL、分析行情，甚至搭实时 Dashboard

每秒摄入百万级事件、毫秒查实时数据，而且现在连 Claude、Codex、Cursor 都能直接接。

我觉得它现在最有意思的地方，是已经不只是“一个很快的时序数据库”。

它开始往 AI Agent 的实时金融数据底座走了。

上面 Agent 做研究、策略和分析，下面 QuestDB 负责把几亿条 Tick、订单簿和历史行情稳稳托住。

做量化交易、Crypto 行情、订单簿研究、高频数据，或者想给自己的 AI Trading Agent 搭数据底座，这个值得留着。

https://t.co/pdKqgTLo3a

quotedTweet.text:
Bloomberg 真正值钱的，不是那块黑底屏幕。

而是你敲几个命令，就能把行情、财报、SEC、期权、新闻、宏观、机构持仓全拉到一个工作台里。

Gloomberb，2.3K Stars，直接把这套“金融终端工作流”开源了。

而且它不是做个 Bloomberg 皮肤，而是真的已经塞了 100+ 个金融功能进去。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 个股研究一站式：行情、K 线、财报、估值、SEC Filing、分析师评级、期权链都能直接查

2️⃣ 宏观也很全：美债收益率曲线、利率路径、信用利差、全球指数、期货持仓、经济日历都做进去了

3️⃣ 机构数据直接看：13F、机构持仓、Insider、基金持仓，不用再来回翻多个网站

4️⃣ 组合和交易工作台也有：Watchlist、Portfolio、Broker 连接、Alert、Notes 都能放在同一个终端里

5️⃣ 操作方式很“彭博”：`DES AAPL` 看公司、`GP NVDA` 开图表、`FA` 看财务、`13F` 看机构，键盘敲命令就走

6️⃣ Desktop + TUI + Browser 都能用，还支持 Plugin 扩展，自己的数据源、Broker、研究工具都可以继续往里塞

我觉得它最爽的一点是：

它不是让你“多装一个看盘软件”。

而是把原来散落在十几个网页里的研究动作，重新收回到一个键盘驱动的工作台里。

而且终端本身 MIT 开源、免费，本地桌面和 TUI 都能跑；需要实时数据、新闻线和财报电话会这些高级数据，再单独上 Cloud Pro。

做美股研究、宏观、期权，或者一直想自己搭一套 Bloomberg 风格金融终端的，这个很值得玩。

GitHub：https://t.co/iwZYEeKn09

2️⃣ 新增 QWP 二进制协议，一条连接同时负责写入和查询，官方峰值达到 1900 万行/秒

3️⃣ SQL 直接为量化准备了 SAMPLE BY、ASOF JOIN、LATEST ON、WINDOW JOIN，算 OHLCV、盘口匹配很顺手

4️⃣ Live Views + Materialized Views 可以边接实时行情边计算指标，不用每次重新扫完整历史数据

5️⃣ 原生支持 Parquet、Arrow、PostgreSQL 协议，Python、Pandas、Polars、Grafana 这些都能直接接

6️⃣ 新版加入 QuestDB Skill + MCP，Claude、Codex、Cursor 可以自己查 Schema、写 SQL、分析行情，甚至搭实时 Dashboard

每秒摄入百万级事件、毫秒查实时数据，而且现在连 Claude、Codex、Cursor 都能直接接。

它开始往 AI Agent 的实时金融数据底座走了。

上面 Agent 做研究、策略和分析，下面 QuestDB 负责把几亿条 Tick、订单簿和历史行情稳稳托住。

做量化交易、Crypto 行情、订单簿研究、高频数据，或者想给自己的 AI Trading Agent 搭数据底座，这个值得留着。

核心能力：

它不是让你“多装一个看盘软件”。

太牛逼了，鱼总居然把推特一年 40 万+ 变现公开了，这么细的东西我是真不太敢发😅。。。

我就先陪一张今年部分海外收入吧，具体细节先不公开了，以后讲😂

X变现这块还得看鱼总，一年从 0 涨到 6.3 万粉：
商单 55-60%，联盟分佣 30-35%，官方收益 5-10%

我和鱼总在 X 变现方面思路差不多，或者说在 X 上，或者自媒体，真赚到钱的基本都这样：
号需要跟真实的变现需要绑在一起，为了流量做流量，除了流量啥也没有（其实，都是细节......）。

干货太多了，刚学习了一下，我来给大家详细讲一讲：
1、涨粉 = 曝光 × 转化
被别人 @、被大V转发，转化率最高，等于有人替你背书；曝光很大却不涨粉，多半是主页没接住。

2、回复最重要，作者自己下场回复权重最高
划走、点不感兴趣、拉黑都算扣分，硬塞标签、卡整点发都没用。怀疑被限流，设置里的 Under the Hood 能自己查。

3、前期千万别进互关群，也别刚发两三条就挂推广链接，很容易被当成营销号。

4、商单当干货写，数据好下一单就能涨价
联盟别等商家上门，主动找自己在用的工具谈，一篇卡类教程就能带来 1000-2000 美元分成。

5、社群和课程他反而不推荐，交付太重，做不好还伤 IP（我也是这样想的，收益很难做高，而且交付太重了）。

兄弟们，别管是推特还是其他各种平台，做起来吧！如果你能坚持三个月肯定会很大的收获！

text:
郭宇在这场分享中关于「高级打工仔」与读书的核心观点，可以概括为以下三层：

一、传统路径已经失效

他明确提出，东亚社会长期推崇的“读书—考名校—成为高级知识打工人”路径，在AI时代已经逐渐失去可行性。

2025年10月Claude Code推出代码生成能力后，医生、律师等依托智力获取超额收益的知识类职业优势被大幅削弱，依靠个人智力做“高级打工人”已经不再是一个可以稳定追求的目标。

背后的逻辑是：你能使用到的智力，和你自己能获取到的智力，已经完全不成比例。

人类花十年读书只能学到皮毛，不可能每天不睡觉学完ChatGPT预训练的所有知识，而且AI还能边做边学，获取前人知识的速度远超人类。

二、读书本身的价值需要重新定义

他并没有否定读书或知识的价值，而是认为读书的目标不能再是“成为高级打工人”。

传统东亚教育的底层逻辑是“读书=不做体力劳动=阶层跨越/经济自由”，这套逻辑在工业时代成立，但在AI时代需要转向，知识不再是用来卖时间、换薪资的筹码，而是用来构建叙事、撬动智能复利的杠杆。

三、AI时代的替代方向：用智能赚复利
他提出的新方向是掌握叙事（narrative）能力，用智能赚取复利，而不是靠单次劳务换取报酬。

核心论据是：

1. AI当前尚不具备自主决定叙事方向的能力，这是人类独有的核心竞争力。

2. JK·罗琳靠《哈利·波特》叙事体系获得的长期收益，远超过影片中小演员的短期劳务收入——这就是智能复利的典型形态。

3. 叙事能力不只是写书，打造服装品牌、运营亚马逊爆款、做AI生成内容、经营个人IP，本质都是讲好故事触达用户，获取长期复利。

AI时代最关键的转变，是把自己从工业革命时代的“螺丝钉”，拔高到能够主导叙事的创造者。

Everyone's posting animations made with Opus 5.5. The one quoted below is the most useful I've seen: a designer who struggled to explain their UX decisions in interviews turned them into an animation with Opus 5.5, 𝗼𝗻𝗲 "𝘄𝗵𝘆" 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽.

Code works the same way. In interviews, PRs and team syncs, the hardest thing to get across is why you chose what you chose: why this database, why the modules are split this way.

The same rhythm works for code decisions too. The animation below is what Claude Code made from 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘁 after reading a sample project's commit history: circle the problem, turn the screen into a blueprint, move only what changes, then land one line on why.

Send this prompt to Claude Code to turn one technical decision in your project into an animation like this 👇

"Turn one technical decision in this project into a roughly 40-second blueprint-style explainer animation: each step circles the problem first, turns the screen into a blueprint, moves only what changes, then ends on one line about why we chose it.

1. Read the recent commits and the related code, list 3 decisions worth explaining, and let me pick one.
2. Once I pick, split it into 3 to 5 steps, following problem → options we considered → trade-offs → final choice, one sentence per step. Show me the storyboard first.
3. After I confirm, build it with HyperFrames (if it isn't installed, set it up from https://t.co/FymJe8Xlht). Use code snippets and architecture diagrams, and make it readable on a phone: keep only the key lines of code and use large text. Cut straight between steps, no black screens. Render it as an MP4.
4. After rendering, grab one frame per second into a contact sheet and check it yourself: no overlapping text, every step clear, and the visuals match what the code actually does. Fix what you find, then show me."

第一次做美股 LP，别看到七巨头就想全开。

先把一只做明白：QQQx-USDC

为什么从它开始？

因为如果你本来就愿意长期持有纳指，LP 可以理解成：
上涨时逐渐卖出一部分 QQQx，下跌时逐渐用 USDC 接回 QQQx，过程中赚取做市手续费。所以它不是“17% 年化理财”。

更准确地说是：用自动做市的方式管理 QQQ 仓位，手续费只是额外补贴。

text:
can someone genuinely explain why you would announce something negative like cutting plan limits before your big highlight event esp when you’ve spent weeks promising a lot & the event itself doesn’t even fully land?

even more confusing when your competitor currently has a better model with much more generous usage & the audience you’re broadcasting to is unusually obsessed with limits.

you’ve also spent months training everyone to care about the reset limits button. then right before the event you make the entire timeline about usage scarcity instead of what you’re about to ship.

why not announce it a day or two later? or at minimum after the event?

instead you create the worst possible framing in which everyone watches the launch asking whether what you shipped justifies what you took away.

maybe i’m missing some sophisticated comms logic here. i’m obviously not a trained comms/pr person (i can’t believe there is training for this either) but i think about this stuff a lot & the sequencing makes zero sense to me. but whatever.

text:
If I was starting a new project from zero today, this is exactly where I’d start.

It doesn’t matter if the project is a business, a family project, research, content, software, or something completely different.

The foundation can stay the same.

THE FOUNDATION

AGENTS.md tells the agents how to operate.

PROJECT.md defines what we’re actually trying to accomplish.

STATUS.md keeps everyone grounded in where the project stands right now.

DECISIONS.md preserves the important choices so they don’t disappear into old conversations.

THE ORGANIZATION

inbox/ gives everything new a temporary landing place.

areas/ breaks the project into whatever major sections naturally make sense for that specific project.

resources/ holds the files, references, assets, notes, data, and other material the project depends on.

THE WORK

work/ separates what’s queued, what’s actively being worked on, and what’s already completed.

outputs/ gives finished or review-ready work a clear destination.

archive/ keeps old or replaced material without cluttering the active project.

THE SCALING PART

This is where it gets useful.

The root AGENTS.md contains the rules that apply to the entire project.

If one area becomes complicated enough, that folder can get its own AGENTS.md with instructions specific to that area.

If it grows again, you can repeat the same pattern another level down.

The goal isn’t to build a massive system on day one.

Start with a universal foundation.

Then specialize downward only when the complexity actually earns it.

text:
微软搞的一个去中心化多AI框架：Agensh，去掉“AI大管家”，让最多1024个Agent自协作，自己商量、分工、干活

结果是人越多越快，128个AI半小时就突破的进度，1个AI 两小时都达不到，有意思的是AI还自发长出了组织能力

随着AI数量增加，涌现出了类似人类社会的现象：
8个AI：先约定接口，然后各自独立开发

32个AI：出现多人评审，发现bug会撤回批准、要求返工

当128个AI：出现专业分工和标准化流程，还发明了一套整合协议（更新+测试+发哈希验证），后来被其他AI复用和修订

当1024个AI：出现专职的“整合者”角色，某个AI失败后会有专长者接手，组织不再依赖任何单一个体

现在的多AI系统一般是“一个老板带一群员工”，老板要负责派活、协调、汇总

Agensh的解法是，不要老板，每个AI都拿到同样的任务说明，然后循环做五件事：

1、看进展，项目做到哪了？别人发现了什么？
2、认领任务，并公开声明（撞车了就和对方私下协商）
3、动手干活，写代码、跑测试
4、自检结果，不达标就继续修
5、提交合并，提交Pull Request，把成果并入主干

配套的是三件套基础设施，很像GitHub工作流：共享工作区（Git管代码和合并冲突）、消息接口（频道公告+私聊，类似Slack）、共享上下文（记录事实、失败教训、任务认领的团队Wiki）

这对费时费力的长时工程倒是一种新解法。在把单个模型做大和让单个模型多想一会儿之间给出了第三条路，固定模型不变，增加Agent数量，让整体能力提升

#Agensh #Agent

text:
Anthropic just published its official guide to Sonnet 5.5. You can ask Claude Code to use it to check which of your work to hand to Sonnet 5.5, which is faster and 𝗵𝗮𝗹𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲, and which to keep on Opus 5.5.

Once you're on Claude Code 2.1.284, any subagent with model: sonnet is 𝗮𝗹𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆 𝗿𝘂𝗻𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝗦𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝘁 𝟱.𝟱 (on the Claude API).

Its effort levels were also recalibrated, so the same level doesn't mean the same amount of thinking as on Sonnet 5. So don't carry over your Sonnet 5 effort settings. For everyday use, start at medium and go to high for harder or longer work. At xhigh or max it thinks longer and costs more, and for that kind of work the guide suggests considering Opus 5.5.

Send this prompt to Claude Code 👇

"Read this guide: https://t.co/PU3Ug5CzMJ

Then review my Claude Code setup against it: my user and project settings, the subagents in ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents, any model set in commands and skills, and CLAUDE.md. If this project has code that calls the Claude API, check that too. Find three kinds of problems:
1. Models doing the wrong work. Flag subagents that set no model and run on my main Opus model when their job is well-scoped, repeated work like investigation, review or drafting; those fit Sonnet 5.5. Long-horizon agentic coding and work that needs careful judgment stays on Opus 5.5. Then look at this project's code and recent commits and tell me which kinds of work here I should switch to with /model sonnet.
2. The wrong effort. List every effort level hard-coded for Sonnet, including subagents with model: sonnet that now run on Sonnet 5.5. Suggest levels from the guide's ladder: medium for well-scoped work, high for harder or longer work, and xhigh or max only where a gain was measured.
3. Settings and instructions that don't work or backfire on Sonnet 5.5: settings that turn thinking off, instructions telling it to 'think less' or to write its reasoning into the reply, and workarounds added for older models, like 'do not be lazy', refusal steering or tool retry prompts. If there's code calling the API, also check for calls that now return a 400 and anything that reads content[0].text; if not, skip this part.

For each issue, quote the setting or line, explain the impact, and suggest the smallest change.

Show me the recommendations first. Don't change anything yet."

Of course, if your usage limits can take it, keeping everything on Opus 5.5 is a fine choice too. I wrote up how to set each Opus 5.5 effort level in my post quoted below 👇

quotedTweet.text:
Anthropic just published its 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗴𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲 for Opus 5.5. You can ask Opus 5.5 to use it to review your Claude Code setup.

At the same effort level, Opus 5.5 thinks more per turn than Opus 5, most of all at xhigh and max. Thinking is billed as output, and an output token costs 𝟭𝟬𝟬 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗰𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱. So don't carry over the level you set for Opus 5. Start at medium, and save xhigh and max for work where you've measured a gain.

Send this prompt to Opus 5.5 👇

"Read this guide: https://t.co/8RHkfmiKjM

Then review my Claude Code setup against it: my user and project settings, the subagents in ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents, CLAUDE.md, and the MCP servers I have connected. Find three kinds of problems:
1. A default effort that doesn't fit the work. Use the guide's ladder: low for mechanical edits, medium for well-scoped daily work, high when medium stalls, and xhigh or max only for work where a gain was measured. Flag a default of xhigh or max, or a level I picked for Opus 5. Then look at this project's code and recent commits and tell me which kinds of work here fit which level.
2. Subagents that only search, read logs or run tests but set no model, so they run on my main model.
3. Setup that makes every turn cost more: MCP servers I don't use, or a CLAUDE.md well over 200 lines.

For each issue, quote the setting or line, explain what it costs, and suggest the smallest change. Also tell me which three things to check in /usage at the end of a task.

Show me the recommendations first. Don't change anything yet."

Anthropic just published its 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗴𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲 for Opus 5.5. You can ask Opus 5.5 to use it to review your Claude Code setup.

At the same effort level, Opus 5.5 thinks more per turn than Opus 5, most of all at xhigh and max. Thinking is billed as output, and an output token costs 𝟭𝟬𝟬 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗰𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱. So don't carry over the level you set for Opus 5. Start at medium, and save xhigh and max for work where you've measured a gain.

Send this prompt to Opus 5.5 👇

"Read this guide: https://t.co/8RHkfmiKjM

Then review my Claude Code setup against it: my user and project settings, the subagents in ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents, CLAUDE.md, and the MCP servers I have connected. Find three kinds of problems:
1. A default effort that doesn't fit the work. Use the guide's ladder: low for mechanical edits, medium for well-scoped daily work, high when medium stalls, and xhigh or max only for work where a gain was measured. Flag a default of xhigh or max, or a level I picked for Opus 5. Then look at this project's code and recent commits and tell me which kinds of work here fit which level.
2. Subagents that only search, read logs or run tests but set no model, so they run on my main model.
3. Setup that makes every turn cost more: MCP servers I don't use, or a CLAUDE.md well over 200 lines.

For each issue, quote the setting or line, explain what it costs, and suggest the smallest change. Also tell me which three things to check in /usage at the end of a task.

Show me the recommendations first. Don't change anything yet."

text:
The agents that run my LinkedIn outreach are currently getting a 55% reply rate on cold outreach and are generating hundreds of signups for me completely on autopilot.

I packaged the exact system into a skill that works for any harness so you can copy it for yourself. https://t.co/P0B8K17M01

Heres why this system prints qualified replies:

most outbound starts with a list out of apollo, zoominfo or clay. firmographics. who could buy. that list is cold on arrival because "could buy" and "is thinking about this right now" are two different lists.

so mine starts from linkedin posts my buyers are already reacting to. that also means every person on the list actually uses linkedin, since they just reacted to a post on it. most people don't, so a message to a normal list mostly sits unread.

across the client accounts i've worked on, an apollo-style list usually gets about 1/10th the reply rate of one built this way.

the posts come from three places: buyers posting about the problem themselves (hiring for it, breaking under it, shopping for a fix), a watchlist of my competitors and the creators my buyers follow, and the topic itself.

when a buyer writes the post, the author is the best lead on it. anyone reacting to a competitor's product post is already shopping.

every search is written in the words buyers actually post in, because vendor jargon only finds other vendors.

it pulls everyone who reacted or commented, drops anyone i've already contacted plus competitors and their staff, and scores each person 0 to 100 against my ICP with the reason written on the row. anyone under the bar is gone before i've paid for their email.

this is the part everyone skips.

for every lead that clears the bar, it reads their website, their LinkedIn profile & anything else it can find about them on the internet, works out what agent would actually help their operation, and builds it. a real one, sitting there, with a claim link.

so i am not sending "quick question about your outbound."

i am sending "i built you an agent that does X for your company, want me to send over the link?"

it sequences that into heyreach for linkedin and instantly for email, then runs the inbox.

anyone who has done outbound knows reply speed is most of the game, and also the exact thing you quit doing by week three.

every reply fires a webhook. it re-reads the whole thread, tags it interested, not interested or auto-reply, pings me in slack the second someone's interested, and sends them their claim link. i don't touch it.

and every reply feeds the next run. it writes more searches like the ones that got answers, so week four sources better than week one.

the general rule, and it has nothing to do with my software:

use AI to build a personalized, genuinely useful asset and give it away in the first message.

you're not hard selling anyone. you are handing them a thing. and because it's built off their actual company, nobody can mistake it for a template. reply rates go up for both reasons at once.

it doesn't have to be an agent. the skill builds whatever your business is already good at making:

- sell lead gen? a sample list of 10 to 25 of their own buyers
- sell SEO? the 3 to 5 searches their competitors win and they don't
- build websites? a teardown of their homepage with three fixes
- consult? a one-page plan for the exact problem they commented about

the playbook behind the messages is the best outbound advice on the internet in one place. it's built from 25 full-length videos and 60 posts from operators who do this at scale, plus 3 production systems running this exact play. scraped the videos and posts with superagnt's data MCP btw.

run it once in claude code or codex and look at what it staged. once you like it, it turns the whole thing into a small agent team on a schedule. the sourcing side runs about 8 cents per qualified lead in production.

grab it here, paste the install prompt into your agent and let it cook: https://t.co/P0B8K17M01

Welcome to the world Taku, Dyna’s real world long horizon Physical AI Agent, the first of its kind.

Getting back to Lindon’s original vision of real world “Performance as the Product” this was the #1 reason we invested in Dyna.

Real world performance is not just a demo as a product or research as a product, it’s real world performance backed by real world customer needs. Research and a frontier robot foundation model is a core part, but not the only part.

As Lindon and team deployed with customers like Din Tai Fung, Best Western, and others who operate on a global scale, these customers were impressed by existing capabilities and wanted more. What they wanted was of course a robot that could replace the whole employee that was high churn (300% annualized churn), unreliable, and costly to employ (including health care, insurance, and other benefits). Anyone who’s managed a restaurant, hotel, or gym/laundry can totally feel the pain of managing unreliable high skill, blue collar working staff.

Dyna simply delivered:

1) Dyna’s frontier robot foundation model (1->2->2.1->more in the future), backed by frontier research into WAM/VLA, in sim RL, real deployment evals, and nimble experimentation with new architectures as needed (eg CUA), etc.
2) Custom hardware coupled to the model for performance. It’s not just the brain but also performant robot control policies required to deliver to customer grade quality and throughput SLAs
3) Data - 1M+ hours of human egocentric data for pre-training and UMI/teleop for mid training/post-training, with finally the last mile deployment to do real world deployment evals and grinding out the edge cases to close out the data flywheel. (Note: You can bet your ass I will be kingmaking Dyna when it comes to the frontier data access and partnerships.)
4) Infrastructure scaling - to support the vast amount of data to training Dyna 2 and future model versions. This is a direct bottleneck to data scale.
5) Go-to-market distribution - real customer traction with production contracts not just for business growth, but also for R&D. Importantly customer selection into the restaurant, hotel, hospitality as a wedge with expansion to more domains, uniquely gives Dyna the first mover advantage in an O(hundreds of billions) to O(trillion) global TAM.
6) The X factor - Lindon’s product and business sense and ability to constantly and adaptively upscope to customer needs. This is what will carry Dyna to become a generational Physical AGI company.

If folks haven’t noticed by now, as with any products that require hardware, Performance as the Product requires expertise across a “multilayered cake” of disciplines that I just summarized above.

And of all the hot robotics startups in Silicon Valley, Dyna is the ONLY one among its relative competitors (Skild, PI, Genesis, Generalist, Sunday et al) with an optimized, balanced approach across the entire stack, led by a generational product and business minded CEO (vs an AI research led CEO with a sprinkle of product/business sense).

QED folks - Dyna in full Mog Mode.

text:
This was pretty interesting to look up and see myself on Space Telescope Live. I also didn't know the details of Space Telescope Live on what you actually see live, depending on which part of the instruments are being turned on. What was scene there is actually not from the Hubble at all, its a background underlay from DSS2 (2nd Generation Digitized Sky Survey) which includes data from various ground telescopes, including Second Palomar Observatory Sky Survey (POSS-II) consequently😂. It's a known artifact from the digitization of photographic glass plates taken from these telescopes at the time. I'll attach some other sources and go over some of the details of why in this 🧵. 

But in summary:
-Anomaly isn't from Hubble but a older background data underlay from DSS2 used in Space Telescope Live. Hubble at the time was calibrating and taking in UV Data, no data from the visual light spectrum at that time.

- Reflections caused by a combination of the star TYC-3779-1567-1 and the gas emissions from that star. During the scanning process of the glass plates of DSS2 data, this anomaly forms due to the glass plates the stars were captured on.  This new technique of scanning the glass plates contributed to this anomaly during the process. Similar strange galaxy and star anomalies can be seen in DSS2 data sets and is a known issue.

-When compared to the DSS1 data set, which was the first scan made from first survey, with glass plates coated with anti-halation coating, the anomaly isn't present in the Far-red spectrum at all. Same star, same constellation, same formation.

-This anomaly can be found in other sources such as on Stellarium and ALADIN, without issues.  Also means it isn't being hidden, and is consistent with Space Telescope Live observations.

-This anomaly in DSS2 has been present since 2000😂.

I can definitely see the improvement from GPT-6 Sol to GPT-6.1 Sol, but a few things stood out to me in this run:

>I explicitly asked the model not to stop for approvals! GPT-6 Sol respected that but GPT-6.1 Sol did not Medium asked once, and High asked repeatedly, which made the experience noticeably more frustrating and also inflated the real wall-clock time.
>The Medium vs High difference is really interesting! Medium actually did better on the hidden-defect benchmark: 9/9 vs 8/9, while High made far more changes, added more tests, and still missed one defect.
>High also took roughly 2–3x longer in real time because of those approval interruptions, even though its reported active work time looked much shorter.
>GPT-6.1 clearly explores more aggressively: more files touched, much more code churn, and many more tests. That can be useful, but it also makes restraint more important and both GPT-6.1 runs still broke GT-10.

Overall though, I do see real progress and going back to my earlier Astra comparison, GPT-6 High already landed in roughly the same range as Astra on this benchmark. 

So when Tibo says GPT-6.1 is around Astra level, that looks believable from my results too. The bigger question for me now is whether, with more time and cleaner autonomy, GPT-6.1 can move beyond that level rather than just doing more work.
